subject: geom_point scale_x_continous Error: No Layers in plot

messages.author: 2cf0e6d7d5f19844
messages.subject: geom_point scale_x_continous Error: No Layers in plot
parts:
Hi,

I have a simple plot that I am working on,  the plot works, but when I add labels or name the plot errors out.  here is the script:

cs <- 10000000
w <- c(400000,300000,200000,100000)
sp <- 1

getQuantity <- function(amount) {
  
  counter <-- 0
  
  q <- cs
  
  mp <- amount/cs
  
  repeat{
    counter <- counter + 1
    
    q2 <- cs + sum(round(w*(mp-sp)/mp))
    
    mp <- amount/q2
    
    if (q2 == q || counter > 500) {
      break
    } else {
      q = q2
    }
    
  }
  
  return(q)
  
}

exitAmount <- seq(from = 10000026, to = 10000026.03, by = .01)
quantities <- lapply(exitAmount,getQuantity)
quantities <- unlist(quantities)
df <- data.frame(exitAmount,quantities)

if (!require("ggplot2")){ 
  install.packages("ggplot2")
} 
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

p <- ggplot(df,aes(x=exitAmount,y=quantities))
p + geom_point()
p + scale_y_continuous(name="Realized Quantity", labels=comma)
p + scale_x_continuous(name="Exit Amount ($)", labels=comma)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: geom_point scale_x_continous Error: No Layers in plot
parts:
You need to do this:

p <- ggplot(df,aes(x=exitAmount,y=quantities))
p + geom_point() +
scale_y_continuous(name="Realized Quantity", labels=comma) +

As you've defined it, p has no layers. Your second line adds a
geom_point() layer, but the third line goes back to p without the
geom_point() layer. Basically, you were trying to define a scale on an
empty plot region. Do it as above and it will work (tested).

Dennis
